name: Grawa-Wasserfall
kurzbeschreibung: The Grawa Waterfall in Neustift im Stubaital: At 85m, the widest waterfall in the Eastern Alps, with a 180m drop, the WildeWasserWeg, and healing spray inhalation.
beschreibung:
Overview

The monumental Grawa Waterfall in the rear Stubai Valley, within the municipality of Neustift im Stubaital, is a natural monument of superlatives. With a cascade width of an impressive 85 meters, it is considered the widest waterfall in the entire Eastern Alps. Fed by the mighty glacier ice masses of the Sulzenauferner in the Stubai Alps, the roaring waters of the Sulzaubach plunge over 180 meters in two powerful drops. Nestled in primeval Swiss pine and larch forests, this natural spectacle, protected since 1979, forms the undisputed heart of the regionally celebrated WildeWasserWeg.

Route & Requirements

This geological monument was formed during the last ice age when the deep trough valleys of the Stubai Valley were carved out. As the ice-cold meltwater crashes onto the hard granite gneiss rocks, the water is atomized into microscopically fine droplets. A groundbreaking clinical study by the Paracelsus Medical Private University Salzburg (PMU), led by Univ.-Doz. Dr. Arnulf Hartl, scientifically proved the extraordinary healing power of this natural phenomenon: the mechanical atomization creates an extremely high concentration of negatively charged ions and respirable nano-aerosols.

Visit & Arrival

The Grawa Waterfall and the observatory are freely and completely accessible free of charge (0.00 € admission) 365 days a year, around the clock. The best time to visit is during the summer months from May to October, when glacier melt reaches its peak and the cascades thunder with maximum water force. In winter, the waterfall transforms into a gigantic work of art made of blue ice. Arrival by public transport: Take VVT bus line 590 (Stubaitalbus) from Innsbruck main station or Fulpmes every half hour directly to the Neustift i. St. Grawa Wasserfall stop (buses stop directly at the starting point). By car: Brenner motorway A13 to the Schönberg/Stubaital exit, then on the B183 Stubaitalstraße via Neustift and Ranalt to the hiking car park at Grawa Alm (paid parking available directly on site).

Tips

Unlike many alpine gorges, the Grawa Waterfall is exemplarily barrier-free: from the bus stop and the Grawa Alm, a wide, flat, and finely gravelled path leads in only about 400 meters (approx. 10 minutes' walk) to the viewing platform; the entire wooden deck of the Grawa Observatory is accessible with wheelchairs and strollers without thresholds. The neighbouring, 400-year-old Grawa Alm also offers a wheelchair-accessible toilet and sunny outdoor seating. Pack a wind and waterproof jacket, as the healing spray can drift finely over the relaxation loungers depending on wind conditions.
oeffnungszeiten: Open all year round (best time to visit May to October)
